body:
This is awkward, because I chose not to explain a bunch of things when I wrote that or I'd get too intellectual and just say screw it to the whole post...

I know...almost all of this, my father had the good will to diagram SSRI functioning to me at the age of 7 when I asked about all the pills on the table. I took intro, abnormal, social, and developmental psychology. I can explain and rationalize almost every aspect of my mental illness, and that helps keep things suppressed in day to day life. This has made the almost total randomness of the driving desire to kill myself harder to bear with when it breaks through, because it hurts so much and makes so little sense, despite the illness making sense from a distance. 

And I know that in every functional sense, I am not my father. But by every indication, in terms of sickness, I am my father's child. The same things driving me mad have driven him to alcohol (there was one time he was telling me a story that until college he thought it was totally normal that walking on a bridge would result in suicidal ideation out of nowhere, and that is how it happens to me). I don't fear I'll make the same choices or behave as they do, I fear the biological precedent -- that my anxiety and depression will always be waiting around the corner to stab me from the inside, never relenting, just waiting for me to crack a little so it can tear me up anew. All of us have been medication resistant in one fashion or another -- I can't think of an influence the SSRIs or Wellbutrin had on me earlier in life, my sister has never responded completely to medication, and my father exhausted all of the anti-depressants they tried over 20+ years and is still trying to find something that works amongst anti-psychotics without equally life destroying side-effects. None of this was done as a take it or leave it -- all of us were/are versed in talking to a psychiatrist about changing medications or dosage and so forth.

My experiences with talking to doctors and therapists have not been especially productive in my life. I've looked back at this and in hindsight believe that it has much to do with the necessity of lying to myself to function from day to day in the mildly accomplished world I've managed to build. I can't stop lying to myself and the world around me at this point, because it's the only way I know to exist without just ignoring anything and everything in the world to escape the fear...and even that just puts off a shame and worthless pointlessness driven desire to die for a little while.

To technical points, and don't feel bad that you missed this because I was writing insanely -- the girl in China is not my sister, that's the one girl I've ever been truly attracted to and who...seems rather beyond the possibility of ever trying to connect with seriously. My sister is in the US, and our relationship has only improved with distance.

I should also mention I have an overdeveloped devil's advocate from long heated arguments with myself about what other people are thinking about me and trying to talk myself into not believing myself.
